prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Draw the agent loop as an ASCII diagram. Name the harness, the LLM, the tool-call s

risks_fired.evidence: Four named sub-elements may prompt a brief 'I'll diagram these four parts' opening, but single-output request, no planning required — preamble is minimal.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional body primer ('Claude may open with a framing sentence — skip to the diagram') if delivery experience shows disruption; low confidence, not blocking.

prompts_findings.prompt_lead: List the tools you have available in this session. One line each.

Explain how you know what tools you can call in this session.

Then explain how MC

risks_fired.evidence: Three sequential moves ('Explain... Then explain... Last, tell me...') may draw a short framing sentence before the first answer, but sits below the 4+-sub-step structural trigger (check_prompts.md §17), and each move is itself an explanation, not an action being narrated-before.
risks_fired.fix_hint: One-line body primer after the fence if preamble disrupts flow in delivery; not blocking.

risks_fired.evidence: 'tell me whether any of them are deferred until you need them' asks Claude to characterize its own opaque tool-loading state, which it cannot literally introspect. Confidence stays low because the clause anchors to a real in-scrollback artifact — Prompt 2's actual returned list — giving Claude concrete evidence to check its claim against rather than a bare self-grade.
risks_fired.fix_hint: If ever promoted: a short body sentence after the fence naming that the deferred-loading answer here is itself unverifiable without /mcp turns the gap into the lesson instead of leaving it implicit — mirrors the maintainer block's own (trainer-facing) watch-for.
